regime.title: Risk regime
regime.explain: Weighted mean of market stress gauges, each a z-score against up to ten years of its own history (the St. Louis index is already standardised; breadth uses a fixed scale). Positive = more stress than usual. Late readings count half.
regime.pending: The latest session leans {regime}; the badge changes once that holds for 2 sessions.
regime.divergence: High-yield spread {hy} on {date}, up {bp} bp from its low of {low} on {lowDate}, while the S&P 500 is still {gap} above its 200-day average. Not part of the score.
regime.rules: ≤ −0.5 → {on} · ≥ +0.75 → {off}. Changes after 2 sessions; VIX above 35 switches at once.

charts.inflationEst: * IMF annual estimate; no monthly number yet.
charts.rateVn: VN: the State Bank's refinancing rate (BIS publishes none).
charts.spreadHistory: Yield spreads over the last two years (pp)
charts.uninvertHint: An inverted curve came before every US recession since the 1960s, but the recession usually started after the curve turned positive again, not while it was still inverted.

macro.trail: Line = path over the last 6 months
macro.noClock: No leading indicators yet. They arrive with the OECD source (npm run fetch -- oecd).
macro.footnote: Grey text under a number = the period it covers. Hover a column name for what it measures and how it is coloured.
macro.vnNote: Vietnam is in no OECD or BIS dataflow: its CPI and GDP come from the Statistics Office's monthly report (read by AI, see the Vietnam page), or from the IMF and the World Bank when those are as recent; the policy rate from the State Bank, the 10-year yield from Thời báo Ngân hàng's daily recap, and unemployment is the IMF's yearly estimate. It has no leading indicator, confidence survey, real effective exchange rate or credit gap.
macro.cliTitle: OECD leading indicator, last 24 months; under each: latest GDP growth y/y
macro.cpiPartsNote: BLS seasonally adjusted indexes via FRED. Arrow = change over three months. Services ex shelter (the Fed's "supercore") follows wages; shelter follows rents with a lag of about a year.
macro.euroNote: Germany, France and Italy share the ECB's rate (the euro-area cell). Real rate above 0 = money is tight.
macro.reerTitle: Real effective exchange rate vs its 10-year average (BIS)
macro.reerHint: Positive = the currency buys more abroad than usual, so exports are less competitive; negative = cheaper than usual.
macro.confHint: Arrow = direction over 3 months. Below 100, grey: more pessimistic than usual.

uneStatus.crit: Up 1 pp or more from its 12-month low

macro.uneNote: Dot = rising from its 12-month low (the Sahm-rule logic). OECD harmonised rates; Brazil is IBGE's 3-month moving average and India MoSPI's monthly survey (from 2025), neither seasonally adjusted, so their dots compare with a year earlier.
macro.debtHint: General government gross debt, % of GDP, IMF estimate. Amber above 90%, red above 120%.
macro.debtSince2019Hint: Change of the debt ratio since 2019, before the pandemic, in percentage points.
macro.balanceHint: General government net lending (+) or borrowing (−), % of GDP, IMF estimate. Deficits beyond 3% amber, beyond 6% red.
macro.creditGapHint: BIS: private credit-to-GDP ratio minus its long-run trend, pp. Above 2 amber, above 10 red: the zone where past credit booms turned into banking crises.
macro.debtFootnote: Gray text under each number = its period. Hover a column header for what it measures and how it is coloured.
macro.signalsHint: one signal alone has often been a false alarm; several at once is what preceded past recessions.
macro.cliDown: Economies with the leading indicator in downturn
macro.cliDownHint: OECD leading indicator below 100 and still falling. A third of the major economies at once is a watch sign for world growth; half is an alarm.
macro.signalsFootnote: US signals except the last row. Hover a signal's name for what it measures.
macro.ownScale: Each cell has its own scale: read the direction, compare levels by the numbers
macro.mapHint: IMF World Economic Outlook estimates for the whole year; Vietnam is outlined. Hover a country for its number, or switch to the table.
macro.noteEmpty: The note is written once a week, on Monday (Vietnam time), from the numbers on this page.
macro.noteNeedsKey: Add AI_API_KEY (a Gemini or Claude key) to .env.local and restart the worker to get the weekly note.
macro.noteCaveat: Written by AI from the numbers on this page only; check the tables before relying on it.
macro.cpiNote: Dot = distance from target: green within 1 pp, amber 1–3 pp above (or deflation), red more than 3 pp above.
macro.giNote: Growth: GDP y/y minus the economy's 2015–19 average (IMF). Inflation: CPI y/y averaged over the same quarter minus the central bank's target. Hover an economy to see its path over the four quarters before.
macro.fiscalNote: Lines at a 3% deficit (the EU's limit) and 90% of GDP debt (past which studies find growth tends to slow). High debt with a big deficit means debt keeps rising and bond markets can push back. IMF estimates for this year.

surprise.growthHint: Jobs, spending, output, business and consumer surveys, housing
surprise.inflationHint: Consumer and producer prices, wages, inflation expectations
surprise.driversHint: Points each release adds to or takes from the index today
surprise.zHint: Actual minus forecast, in the indicator's typical misses. Green: good news for the economy (stronger growth, cooler prices); red: the opposite.
surprise.note: Actuals and consensus forecasts from Nasdaq's economic calendar, {count} US indicators, latest release {date}. Each release's miss is divided by the indicator's typical miss since 2023; the index is the weighted mean over the last three months, a release counting half as much every 30 days, × 100: 0 = in line with forecasts, +100 = one typical miss above them on average. Built the way Citi builds its surprise index; it is not Citi's index.

map.alertsHint: Click one to zoom in on the map.

news.untagged: Topics appear once the AI pass runs (needs AI_API_KEY)

brief.empty: The brief is written each morning at 06:00 (Vietnam time) once there are enough headlines.
brief.needsKey: Add AI_API_KEY (a Gemini or Claude key) to .env.local and restart the worker to get an AI brief.
brief.requested: Requested — the worker will write it in a few minutes (at most one rewrite every 10 minutes).

highlights.empty: Nothing stands out in the indicators right now.
highlights.needsKey: Add AI_API_KEY to .env.local to get an AI explanation for each one.
highlights.rules: A tile with a line at the bottom stands out: it has just crossed its watch or danger level, moved at least twice its usual size in a session or over a week, or hit a 1-year high or low; the line is written by AI. A level crossed long ago counts less as time passes. Click a tile for the history and the full note.

themes.heatTip: {means} Score {heat}: the gauges' moves over about a month, in units of their usual monthly move.
themes.sinceTip: Change since {date}; {heat}× its usual size, toward {dir}
themes.notCounted: Not counted in the status (history too short or data late)
themes.noNews: No matching headlines in the last two days.
themes.rules: Status: the mean of the gauges' moves over about a month (a month for daily data, the latest release for monthly data), each divided by its usual monthly move over two years; at least +0.5 is heating up, −0.5 or below cooling. Vietnam readings are shown but not counted. Themes are set in config/themes.ts.
themes.needsKey: Add AI_API_KEY to .env.local for a short AI note on each theme.

whatsNew.firstVisit: First visit here: the last 24 hours
whatsNew.rules: Logged by the worker every 15 minutes: risk-regime and theme status changes, indicators newly past their watch or danger level, unusual moves (at least twice the usual size in a session or a week), data releases with the actual against the forecast, and newly exploited vulnerabilities (CISA KEV) at the companies this dashboard follows. Your last visit is kept in this browser only.
whatsNew.dayUp: {name}: unusual jump in a session, {change} ({z}× the usual)
whatsNew.dayDown: {name}: unusual drop in a session, {change} ({z}× the usual)
whatsNew.weekUp: {name}: big rise over the week, {change} ({z}× the usual)
whatsNew.weekDown: {name}: big fall over the week, {change} ({z}× the usual)
whatsNew.standingOut: {n} indicators standing out are in Vital signs

vn.fuelNote: Petrolimex retail prices, ₫ per litre. Zone 2 is remote areas. Prices follow the government's weekly adjustment; the arrow is the change at the last adjustment (red = dearer), shown once one has been recorded here.
vn.bandHint: The State Bank sets a central rate every day; banks may trade the dollar within ±5% of it. A bank rate pressed against the ceiling means the State Bank must sell dollars from its reserves or let the band move.
vn.foreignSums: Net over 5 sessions {s5} · 20 sessions {s20} · this year {ytd}
vn.foreignChart: Foreign net buying on HOSE, last 40 sessions
vn.foreignNote: Order-matched and put-through trades by foreign investors on HOSE, VNDirect data; today's bar moves during the session. Persistent selling weighs on large caps and on the dong.
vn.vn30Note: Area = market cap (price × shares outstanding), color = today's change. Prices from SSI iBoard, shares from VNDirect.
vn.premiumTitle: SJC premium over world gold, million ₫/tael
vn.p2pHint: How much more people pay for a dollar outside the banking system. A gap that widens is dollar demand the banks are not meeting, the clearest early sign of pressure on the dong.
vn.historyNote: SJC, Vietcombank and P2P prices are only stored from late October 2026, so these charts lengthen day by day.
vn.realRateHint: The State Bank's refinancing rate minus the latest CPI inflation. Positive = money is tight; negative = still loose.
vn.outlookNote: Yearly numbers from the IMF: this year is its estimate, later years are forecasts (italic). Last column: emerging and developing economies.

monthly.creditSince: since the end of last year
monthly.gdpQuarter: quarter on the same quarter a year earlier
monthly.growthChart: Growth on a year earlier, by month
monthly.note: Read by AI from the report of {month} ({link}, {date}). Each figure is kept only if it appears word for word in the report, in a sentence that names the measure and the month, within a plausible range; exports − imports must equal the stated balance. Credit and GDP come with the quarterly reports. Preliminary numbers, not revised later.

vn.ratesNote: The gap between the lines is the real rate: the refinancing rate above inflation means money is tight. The National Assembly's inflation target is about 4.5%. CPI: IMF, from the Statistics Office; rate: the SBV's decisions.
vn.regionRank: VN-Index is {rank} of {n} Asia-Pacific markets this year.
vn.regionNote: Each index in its own currency, since the last close of last year. Hover a bar for the index name.
vn.hazardsEmpty: No storm, earthquake, flood or fire recorded near Vietnam in the last 14 days.
vn.hazardsNote: Storms are tracked out to the Philippine Sea (0–30°N, 100–135°E); other hazards within 5–25°N, 100–118°E. Distance to the nearest of Hanoi, Da Nang and Ho Chi Minh City. GDACS, NASA EONET, USGS.

markets.summary: {up} of {n} markets up in their latest session · best {best} · worst {worst}
markets.note: Day = each exchange's latest session, open or closed. Green deepens with the size of a rise, red with a fall, on each column's own scale. In local currency, so currency moves are not included.
markets.summaryCommodities: {up} of {n} up in their latest session · best {best} · worst {worst}
markets.noteCommodities: Front-month futures, each in its contract's unit (¢ = US cents). Energy and food reach consumer prices in importing countries within months, Vietnam included.
markets.noteAssets: Change since last year's final close, in each asset's own currency (VN-Index in dong). World and emerging-market stocks and Treasuries are ETFs (ACWI, EEM, IEF): price only, without dividends or coupons.

cot.netHint: Contracts held long minus short by the group, as of Tuesday
cot.pctOiHint: Net position as a share of all open contracts
cot.weekHint: Change in the net position since the previous report, contracts
cot.rankHint: Where the net position (% of open interest) ranks among the last 156 weeks: 0 = the most short, 100 = the most long
cot.historyHint: Net position as % of open interest, weekly over three years

groupHints.mm: CTAs and hedge funds trading commodity futures
groupHints.am: Pension, insurance and mutual funds; leveraged funds' short in Treasuries is mostly the cash–futures basis trade, so this side reads as the view on rates

cot.extremeHint: In the top or bottom 10% of the last three years. When one side is this full, a surprise can force a sharp unwind.
cot.summaryNone: No market is at either end of its three-year range.
cot.note: CFTC Commitments of Traders, futures only: positions on Tuesday {date}, published the following Friday afternoon (US time). K = thousand, M = million contracts.

crypto.etfDay: {day}: net flow into spot bitcoin ETFs
crypto.etfChart: Daily net flows of US spot bitcoin ETFs, $M
crypto.etfNote: Net creations minus redemptions of the US spot bitcoin ETFs, $ million, from bitbo.io's table (about ten trading days, so the chart lengthens from late October 2026). A day bitbo has not filled shows as 0 or is missing.
crypto.levTitle: BTC price and perpetual open interest, first day = 100
crypto.lsrHint: Accounts holding a net long BTC perpetual per account holding a net short, on Binance. Far above its average = the crowd leans long, the side that gets squeezed in a sell-off.
crypto.fundingHint: What longs pay shorts (positive) or the reverse, per day on average, as a yearly rate. High funding = paying up for leverage.
crypto.levNote: Binance BTCUSDT perpetual, daily. Open interest counted in coins, so a price move alone does not change it: open interest rising faster than price is leverage building; rising while price falls is new shorts. Binance serves only 30 days, so the chart lengthens from 12 Oct 2026.
crypto.feesWowHint: Fees paid on the chain over the last 7 days against the 7 days before.
crypto.chainsNote: The 10 chains with the most value locked in DeFi (DefiLlama). TVL falls with token prices as well as withdrawals; fees show where people actually pay to use a chain.
crypto.fngNote: Extremes have often coincided with local bottoms (fear) and tops (greed).
crypto.fundingNote: Positive funding = longs pay shorts: leverage leans bullish. Very high funding and fast-rising open interest often precede liquidation flushes.
crypto.p2pNote: Median of the 10 best ads on each side. Ads carry their own limits and requirements, so the two sides can cross.
crypto.unavailable: Not available from this server's location
crypto.noOdds: No long-dated crypto markets right now, or Polymarket is unreachable from this network.
crypto.mapLabel: Top coins sized by market cap, colored by 24-hour change
crypto.mapNote: Area = market cap; fill = 24-hour change: light from ±1%, medium from ±3%, deep from ±6%, grey in between. Stablecoins and wrapped tokens left out. Hover for size and 7-day change; click for CoinGecko.
crypto.ethBtcNote: A rising line means ether beats bitcoin. Traders read a sustained rise as the start of an "altcoin season", when money rotates out of bitcoin into riskier coins. Daily closes from Yahoo Finance.

tech.computeGrowth: Frontier training runs have grown about {x}× a year since 2018 ({n} frontier models).
tech.computeNote: Epoch AI's notable models ({n} with a compute estimate), training compute in FLOP; bars are linear against the largest. Frontier = in the top 10 by compute when released. Many recent models publish no figure and are missing; Epoch's numbers are estimates.
tech.pkgNote: Downloads per complete week, Monday to Sunday UTC (npm downloads API; pypistats.org without mirrors). Downloads count CI runs and installs, not people; read the trend, not the level. Sparkline: 26 weeks.
tech.kpChart: Planetary Kp index, 3-hour steps, last 4 days and the forecast
tech.kpNote: NOAA SWPC planetary Kp, 0–9, every 3 hours; faded bars are the forecast. Dashed lines: Kp 5 (G1 storm) and Kp 7 (G3: GPS errors, HF radio loss, satellite drag, aurora far south).
tech.valueX: Blended price, $ per million tokens (3 in : 1 out)
tech.valueNote: Rating: LMArena text leaderboard, overall, best variant of each model (people vote between two anonymous answers), {date}. Price: OpenRouter's list price; the axis is logarithmic. Lines split at the medians of the models shown. Models OpenRouter does not sell are left out.
tech.noteEmpty: The note is written once a week (Vietnam time) from this page's stories and numbers.
tech.noteCaveat: Written by AI from this page's headlines and numbers only; open the stories before relying on it.
tech.twNote: Taiwan-listed companies report each month's revenue by the 10th of the next (TWSE OpenAPI): AI chip and server demand a month after the fact, long before quarterly results. Only the latest month is published, so history builds up here.
tech.devVsAll: Software postings {dev} against {all} for all jobs (Indeed, 1 Feb 2020 = 100).
tech.eolNote: endoflife.date and the npm registry. Red: a supported line reaches end of life within 30 days, after which it gets no security fixes.
tech.capNote: Market caps in US$; Asian listings converted at today's exchange rate. Prices in each market's own currency.
tech.unreadable: Status page could not be read
tech.statusNote: From each provider's public status page. An incident in a single region counts too, so read where it is.
tech.modelsSummary: {n} models listed in 30 days · {open} with open weights
tech.modelsNote: Price in US$ per million tokens. Date is when OpenRouter listed the model; :free and :batch variants are left out.
tech.papersNote: Hugging Face Daily Papers from the last 3 days, most upvoted first.
tech.modelsTrendNote: Quantized copies and repackagings of other models are left out.
tech.kevSummary: {n} exploited flaws added in 30 days · {r} used in ransomware
tech.kevNote: Every flaw here is being exploited in the wild. The deadline is the one CISA sets for US federal agencies; elsewhere, patch sooner.
tech.noKev: No new entries in the last 30 days.
tech.mapLabel: Tech stocks sized by market cap, colored by the day's change
tech.mapNote: Area = market cap in US dollars; fill = the latest session's change: light from ±0.5%, medium from ±1.5%, deep from ±3%, grey in between. Hover for the year-to-date change.
tech.longTitle: Long-running outages, open more than 14 days ({n})
tech.kevVendorsSummary: {total} flaws added in {days} days; the top three vendors account for {share}%.
tech.kevVendorsLabel: Exploited flaws added per vendor, last {days} days
tech.kevVendorHint: {vendor}: {n} flaws added, {r} known to be used in ransomware
tech.kevVendorsNote: A vendor with many entries is a favoured target, often because its products sit on the network edge (VPNs, firewalls, file transfer). It is not a ranking of code quality: widely deployed software draws more attackers.

calendar.fredScheduled: Scheduled (FRED); forecast shows in the week of release
calendar.resultHint: Actual computed from FRED data once released; may differ by 0.1 from the published figure because of rounding. Green = better news for the economy than forecast (stronger jobs and growth, cooler inflation), red = worse.
calendar.empty: Nothing scheduled in the next three weeks.
calendar.vn30fDetail: Third Thursday of the month; the trading day before when that is a holiday.
calendar.gsoDetail: CPI, industrial output, retail sales, trade, FDI
calendar.gsoQuarter: CPI, trade, FDI, plus GDP for quarter {q}
calendar.electionExpected: Deadline or likely date, not yet fixed

geo.shipsHint: Average ships a day over the last 7 days of data
geo.historyHint: Weekly average ships a day since January 2023
geo.disruptedHint: Under half the traffic of a year earlier
geo.chokeNote: Ships counted from satellite AIS positions by the IMF's PortWatch, updated weekly; data to {date}.
geo.gprNote: Share of newspaper articles on war, terrorism and tension that name the country (Caldara & Iacoviello), against its own history; sorted by the last three months. Iran is not covered. Small countries swing a lot from month to month because few articles name them.
geo.policyNote: OFAC's recent actions the day they happen; Commerce, the Trade Representative and the President as published in the Federal Register.

trending.vnGoogleNote: Rising searches in Vietnam over the last 24 hours, by Google's search count (a lower bound).
trending.vnVneNote: VnExpress's most-read articles of the last 24 hours.
trending.vnWikiNote: Yesterday's most-read pages, keeping only those read at least 4 times more than usual: the plain ranking is mostly bot traffic.

prediction.fed: Fed funds rate after the {date} meeting
prediction.fedNote: Kalshi: probability the upper bound ends above each level
prediction.filterNote: Odds of 97% or more, or 3% or less, are hidden; the biggest moves in 24 hours come first.
